title: Lua engine callback registration registry findings
scope: Callback registration registry: Lua-side declarations for C++-fired `_on*` callbacks, bounded away from lua_State lifecycle (6A) and deferred scheduler internals (6C).

binaryAnchors.name: LuaClassRegistry_FUN_0078E3A0
binaryAnchors.role: Registers root Lua class globals and script paths.

binaryAnchors.name: std_string_ctor_FUN_00447260
binaryAnchors.role: Builds the callback-name std::string; not a dispatcher by itself.

binaryAnchors.name: LuaCallbackDispatcher_FUN_00CC7A90
binaryAnchors.role: Maps target/control object then invokes callback name plus args.

binaryAnchors.name: LuaProgFuncCallbackFirer_FUN_00CDA690
binaryAnchors.role: Fires embedded prog-function `_onProgFunc` through Lua VM helpers, not through the class/prototype callback dispatcher.

binaryAnchors.name: LuaProgFuncReservedNameLoader_FUN_00D099B0
binaryAnchors.role: Loader/reserved-name checker for `__lge_defineWork`, `__lge_setLoopInterval`, `_progFunc`, and `_onProgFunc`; not a callback fire site.
binaryAnchors.evidence: agent_a_followups_decomp.txt shows FUN_00D07E10 checks over the four reserved names.

callbackDeclarationSurvey.assignmentPattern: L0_1._onName = L1_1 after L0_1 is assigned to a class table

binaryOnlyResolution.luaCorpusLiteralSearch: No `_onProgFunc` literal was found under build/lua. One `_progFunc` reference exists in build\lua\3yv89y_p.lua inside the `_getLanguage` inline wrapper.

representativeDeclarations.notes: Fallback root declarations for common lifecycle/data callbacks.
_onChangeJob at line 1508 pairs with the JobChangeReceiver C++ fire path.
_onPreEvent and _onPostEvent are the Lua handler side for the deferred event-condition firers documented in the deferred-napi-writers pass.
The Talk/Push handlers dispatch into C++ N-API mutators or server-RPC helpers after FUN_00CC7A90 resolves the callback.

registryModel.summary: Creates/registers root class globals and pairs them with script paths.
Loads/decompiles standard Lua 5.1 bytecode; executing the chunk assigns callback closures to class tables.
Handlers register as class-table fields, e.g. CharaBaseClass._onChangeJob = closure.
C++ builds a callback-name string and dispatches by name against the target Lua object.

negativeFindings.finding: No standalone native callback-name registry was identified.
negativeFindings.basis: FUN_0078E3A0 carries class/path records, while individual C++ firers carry their own `_on*` literals. The Lua handler side is visible as prototype assignments in decoded script bytecode.

negativeFindings.finding: FUN_00447260 alone is not a fire site.
negativeFindings.basis: BCS-Y-0311 identifies it as a std::string constructor; FUN_00CC7A90 must be present to complete the Lua dispatch.

negativeFindings.finding: `_onProgFunc` is not a missing shipped Lua-side class/prototype declaration.
negativeFindings.basis: The `build\lua` corpus contains no `_onProgFunc` literal. The two binary xrefs resolve to FUN_00CDA690 (actual embedded prog-function firer through Lua VM helpers, reached by wrapper FUN_00CC77C0) and FUN_00D099B0 (reserved-name loader check). `_onProgFunc` is the entry function name for two embedded `.rdata` Lua chunks outside the shipped `.lpb` class-table callback declarations.
